meta.title: From Xinjiang polysilicon to US solar imports: the Trina Solar chain
meta.heroLede: We followed solar modules imported by Trina Solar's US companies back through factories in Vietnam, Thailand and China to a polysilicon plant in Xinjiang that is on the US government's forced-labour Entity List. Shipment records prove some links. Others rest on indicators. One trail runs cold.
meta.storyTitle: From a Texas factory gate to the Xinjiang desert
meta.storyIntro: Scroll to walk the chain backwards, one tier at a time. Each step says which records support it and how sure we can be.

trina-vn-wafer.role: Trina wafer plant in Vietnam (city not returned; shown at country level). Its Tradeverifyd polysilicon suppliers are outside Xinjiang: Germany, US, Malaysia, Inner Mongolia and Henan. Shown for contrast.
trina-vn-wafer.plainRole: Buys its polysilicon from suppliers outside Xinjiang.

wacker.role: Non-Xinjiang polysilicon supplier (HS 2804.61) to Trina Solar (Vietnam) Wafer in Tradeverifyd (city not returned; shown at country level). Shown for contrast.

flags.label: UFLPA Entity List
flags.detail: Listed by DHS on 21 June 2022 under the 'made with forced labor' sub-list. Renamed 'Xinjiang Goens Energy Technology' in the 3 Aug 2026 update, which is the date Tradeverifyd records for the current listing.

flags.label: BIS Entity List
flags.detail: Added to the Commerce Department's export-control Entity List in June 2021. Tradeverifyd records it as valid from 2021-06-24.

flags.label: XUAR location
flags.detail: Sayari risk factors for Xinjiang geospatial location, registration, operations and name.

flags.label: Law enforcement action (historic)
flags.detail: Sayari risk factors law_enforcement_action and law_enforcement_action_historic (adverse media).

xj-gcl.name: Xinjiang GCL New Energy Material Technology Co., Ltd.
xj-gcl.alias: Xinjiang Goens Energy Technology Co., Ltd. (新疆戈恩斯能源科技有限公司)
xj-gcl.plainRole: Makes polysilicon, the super-pure silicon inside solar cells. It is on a US government list of companies linked to forced labour.

trina-us.plainRole: Brings finished solar panels into the United States.

trina-us-mfg.plainRole: Received solar panels shipped from Vietnam in 2024.

trina-vn.plainRole: Puts solar panels together and ships them to the US.

trina-th.plainRole: Puts solar panels together and ships them to the US.

trina-cn.plainRole: The Chinese parent company. It makes solar cells and runs the factories abroad.

tcl-zhonghuan.plainRole: Slices silicon into thin wafers, the base of every solar cell.

maxeon.plainRole: Another panel company that buys wafers from the same supplier.

jiangsu-zhongneng.plainRole: Owns the Xinjiang polysilicon plant, according to company records.

gaojia-hk.plainRole: Sits higher up the ownership chain of the Xinjiang plant.

gcl-solar-power-hk.plainRole: Sits higher up the ownership chain of the Xinjiang plant.

gcl-poly.plainRole: The listed parent group, according to one dataset only.

hoshine.plainRole: Melts quartz rock into raw silicon. It is on the US forced-labour list, but we found no record linking it to this chain.

hoshine.label: CBP Withhold Release Order (2021)
hoshine.detail: CBP issued a WRO on Hoshine's silica-based products, and goods such as polysilicon made from them, on 24 June 2021.

story.title: A pallet of panels arrives for a factory in Texas
story.body: Vietnamese customs records show monocrystalline solar modules shipped from Hanoi to Los Angeles on 17 September 2024, consigned to Trina Solar's US module plant in Wilmer, Texas. Sayari's supply-chain trace also shows Trina Solar (U.S.) receiving HS 8541 solar goods from 2021 to 2024.

story.title: Built in Vietnam and Thailand
story.body: The modules came from Trina factories in Thai Nguyen, Vietnam and Rayong, Thailand. Southeast Asia matters here: Malaysia, Vietnam and Thailand are the top origins by value of shipments US Customs has stopped under the forced-labour law.

story.title: Back to Changzhou
story.body: Trina Solar Co., Ltd., the Chinese parent, is named as shipper on some US-bound solar shipments between Sept 2023 and Feb 2024. Tradeverifyd annotates it with a human-rights risk flag citing Sheffield Hallam research. Sayari flags it as possibly owning a Xinjiang-based entity, though which entity was not identified.

story.title: The trail turns amber
story.body: Tradeverifyd records Trina Solar Co. as a trade customer of TCL Zhonghuan, a wafer maker in Tianjin. This is a recorded trade relationship, but no shipment-level records, volumes or dates came back, so the link is suspected, not verified.

story.title: Into Xinjiang
story.body: Tradeverifyd lists TCL Zhonghuan as the only outbound trade relationship of Xinjiang GCL, a polysilicon producer in Changji, Xinjiang. Xinjiang GCL has been on the UFLPA Entity List since June 2022. Under the law, goods made wholly or partly by a listed entity are presumed to be made with forced labour and are barred from US import unless the importer proves otherwise.

story.title: Who owns the polysilicon plant?
story.body: Registry data in Sayari shows Xinjiang GCL's shareholder is Jiangsu Zhongneng. Above that sit two Hong Kong companies in the GCL group. No ownership percentages were returned. Tradeverifyd also names GCL-Poly as the parent, but only from a non-registry source.

story.title: Where the trail runs cold
story.body: Hoshine, a silicon-metal giant in Shanshan, Xinjiang, is on the UFLPA Entity List and was hit with a US detention order in 2021. But we found no record of it supplying Xinjiang GCL. The only path between them in Sayari runs through a state-owned construction contractor, which is not a supply relationship. We show this gap rather than fill it.

story.title: A cleaner route is on record, too
story.body: Trina's own wafer plant in Vietnam lists polysilicon suppliers outside Xinjiang, including Wacker in Germany and Hemlock in the US. But no record shows those wafers reaching the Vietnam module plant that ships to Texas. Clean inputs only help if you can trace them into the product.

story.title: Exposed, not proven
story.body: The import end of the chain is documented. The China end rests on trade-relationship indicators that point to a UFLPA-listed Xinjiang polysilicon maker. That is serious exposure under US law, but the records cannot show that any specific panel contains Xinjiang polysilicon. Closing that gap takes shipment-level tracing.

findings.title: Trina Solar's US imports have a recorded trade route back to a UFLPA-listed Xinjiang polysilicon maker
findings.summary: Shipment records document the import end of the chain. Upstream in China, Tradeverifyd records trade relationships from Trina's parent to TCL Zhonghuan, and from TCL Zhonghuan to Xinjiang GCL. These are indicators, not shipment proof.
verified: HS 8541 solar shipments from Trina's Vietnam and Thailand plants to Trina Solar (U.S.), 2021–2024 (Sayari supply-chain trace)
Trina Solar Co., Ltd. named as shipper on HS 8541 goods to Trina Solar (U.S.), Sept 2023 – Feb 2024
Xinjiang GCL has been on the UFLPA Entity List since 21 June 2022
suspected: TCL Zhonghuan → Trina Solar Co.: recorded trade relationship with no shipment-level detail (Tradeverifyd)
Xinjiang GCL → TCL Zhonghuan: TCL Zhonghuan is Xinjiang GCL's only recorded outbound trade relationship (Tradeverifyd)
missing: Shipment-level records (dates, volumes) for either China-side link
Which wafers and cells went into the specific modules shipped to the US
A registry record linking Trina's parent to its Vietnam module plant
findings.why: The UFLPA presumes goods made wholly or partly by a listed entity are made with forced labour. An importer can only rebut that with documentation tracing inputs back to source, which is the very data missing here.
findings.plain: Panels sold in the US can be traced, on paper, back to a blacklisted factory in Xinjiang. The US end is proven; the China end is only suspected.

findings.title: The polysilicon maker is on two US government lists and sits inside Xinjiang
findings.summary: Xinjiang GCL New Energy Material Technology (now listed as Xinjiang Goens Energy Technology) is on both the UFLPA Entity List and the Commerce Department's Entity List. Its registry ownership runs through the GCL group.
verified: UFLPA Entity List since 21 June 2022, renamed in the 3 Aug 2026 update
Sayari location, registration and operations risk factors place it in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region
Shareholder: Jiangsu Zhongneng, owned in turn by two GCL-group Hong Kong companies (Sayari registry data)
suspected: GCL-Poly Energy Holdings as group parent (Tradeverifyd legacy data, not a registry record)
missing: A third shareholder Sayari returned for Jiangsu Zhongneng, not modelled here
findings.why: Sheffield Hallam's research linked all four Xinjiang polysilicon makers, GCL among them, to state labour-transfer programmes.
findings.plain: The polysilicon plant at the end of the trail is on two US government blacklists and is located in Xinjiang.

findings.title: Inside China, the chain goes dark
findings.summary: The links that matter most, wafers and polysilicon moving between Chinese companies, have no shipment-level records in either dataset. The trade relationships also carry HS 8541 (cells and modules) rather than 2804.61 (polysilicon), which suggests aggregated or mis-coded data.
verified: Two Vietnam customs records (17 Sept 2024) of modules consigned to Trina's Wilmer, TX plant, declared at about US$741 and US$630 (likely samples)
suspected: China-side trade relationships recorded at company level only
missing: Shipment records for TCL Zhonghuan → Trina Solar Co.
Shipment records for Xinjiang GCL → TCL Zhonghuan
The wafer and cell source of the Vietnam module plant
Shipment counts for the US-bound legs (Sayari reported 6,441 rows for one query, but only 2 were retrieved)
findings.why: Domestic Chinese trade rarely appears in customs data, which is exactly why the UFLPA puts the burden of proof on the importer.
findings.plain: The most important links, inside China, have no shipping records anyone can check.

findings.title: Trina's parent carries several independent risk flags
findings.summary: Both datasets flag Trina Solar Co., Ltd. These flags describe risk signals about the company. They do not establish what is inside any particular product.
verified: Tradeverifyd annotation: DoD Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies (valid from 8 June 2026)
Tradeverifyd annotation: human-rights violation risk, citing Sheffield Hallam 'In Broad Daylight' research
suspected: Sayari: possibly owns a Xinjiang-based entity within three ownership hops (the entity was not identified)
Sayari: Thailand plant possibly owned by a Section 1260H entity (inferred path)
missing: Identity of the Xinjiang-based entity Sayari's flag refers to
Registry ownership of the Vietnam and Thailand plants
findings.why: The 1260H list concerns links to China's military, not forced labour. It's shown because it affects US procurement risk, not as forced-labour evidence.
findings.plain: Trina's Chinese parent company has several warning flags in both databases.

findings.title: Hoshine: listed and detained, but not linked
findings.summary: Hoshine, the Xinjiang silicon-metal producer at the centre of the 2021 detention order, is the obvious next upstream suspect. We found no record tying it to this chain.
verified: CBP Withhold Release Order on Hoshine silica-based products, 24 June 2021
missing: Any trade record of Hoshine supplying Xinjiang GCL
Sayari's only path between them runs through a state-owned construction contractor, which is not a supply link
findings.why: We show what we looked for and didn't find. Filling the gap with an assumption would make the investigation less trustworthy, not more.
findings.plain: A second blacklisted Xinjiang company is nearby, but we found no record linking it to this chain.

findings.title: A non-Xinjiang polysilicon route exists in the same group
findings.summary: Trina's Vietnam wafer plant lists polysilicon suppliers in Germany, the US, Malaysia and other parts of China. None are in Xinjiang.
suspected: Wacker, Hemlock, OCI and other HS 2804.61 suppliers to Trina Solar (Vietnam) Wafer (Tradeverifyd trade relationships)
missing: Whether those wafers reach the Vietnam module plant that ships to the US. Tradeverifyd links the wafer plant to Hanwha Q Cells Malaysia instead
findings.why: Traceability standards such as SEIA's and the Solar Stewardship Initiative's exist to prove which route a given panel took.
findings.plain: Trina also buys silicon from outside Xinjiang, but we can't tell which silicon ends up in which panel.

extra_gaps: Individual shareholders of Trina Solar Co., Ltd. returned by Sayari are not shown on this site.
Tradeverifyd returned an affiliate link between Maxeon and TCL Zhonghuan whose direction could not be confirmed, so it is omitted.
notes: Neither Sayari nor Tradeverifyd returned coordinates. Map positions are approximate, at city level, or at country level where only a country was given. Maxeon and GCL-Poly had no location and are not on the globe.

present.title: Who made the sunlight?
present.text: Solar panels fight climate change. But the silicon inside many of them comes from a region where the US government says people are forced to work. We followed one real supply chain to see how close that risk gets.

present.title: Almost half came from one place
present.text: In 2020, about 45% of the world's solar-grade polysilicon, the purified silicon inside solar cells, was made in Xinjiang, China.

stat.label: of the world's solar silicon was made in Xinjiang (2020)

present.title: So the US made a law
present.text: Since June 2022, US law assumes that anything made in Xinjiang, or by a company on a government blacklist, was made with forced labour. The importer has to prove otherwise, or the goods are stopped at the border.

stat.label: of solar panels and cells stopped at the US border under this law (Reuters, Feb 2026)

present.title: Every line has a colour
present.text: Each line we draw is a link between two companies. Its colour tells you how sure we are about that link.

present.title: Panels arrive in the USA
present.text: Trina Solar's US companies, including a factory in Texas, receive solar panels from overseas.

present.title: Made in Vietnam and Thailand
present.text: Shipping records show the panels came from Trina's own factories in Vietnam and Thailand between 2021 and 2024.

present.title: Run from China
present.text: Trina Solar's headquarters in Changzhou, China, is named as the shipper on some of these US-bound shipments.

present.title: The trail turns orange
present.text: Trade data says Trina buys wafers, thin slices of silicon, from TCL Zhonghuan in Tianjin. But no shipping records prove it.

present.title: Into Xinjiang
present.text: Trade data also says TCL Zhonghuan buys from Xinjiang GCL, a polysilicon plant on the US forced-labour blacklist since 2022. Again, no shipping records prove it.
present.evidence: Trade data (Tradeverifyd) and the US government blacklist

present.title: Where the trail goes cold
present.text: Hoshine, a silicon smelter nearby, is also on the blacklist. But we found no record that it supplies this chain, so we show the gap instead of guessing.
present.evidence: We searched both databases and found nothing

present.title: Owned through Hong Kong
present.text: Company records show the Xinjiang plant is owned by a GCL company in Jiangsu, which in turn is owned by GCL companies in Hong Kong.

present.title: Exposed, but not proven
present.text: The US end of this chain is proven by records, but the China end is only suspected. That is a real risk under US law. Still, nobody outside these companies can prove what is inside a single panel.

present.title: Trace every panel back to the rock
present.text: The fix is full traceability: records for every step, from quartz rock to finished panel. Industry standards for this already exist, and buyers can demand them.

glossary.polysilicon: Super-pure silicon. It is the key raw material inside almost every solar panel.
glossary.wafer: A thin slice cut from a block of polysilicon. Solar cells are made from wafers.
glossary.cell: The part of a panel that turns sunlight into electricity.
glossary.module: The finished solar panel: many cells framed together.
glossary.importer: The company that brings goods into the US and is responsible for them at the border.
glossary.uflpa: The Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (US law, 2021). It assumes goods made in Xinjiang, or by listed companies, involve forced labour unless the importer proves otherwise.
glossary.entity-list: A US government blacklist of companies. Goods from listed companies are presumed to be made with forced labour.
glossary.xinjiang: A region in northwest China (also called the XUAR or Uyghur Region) where the US and researchers have documented state-run forced labour.
glossary.wro: Withhold Release Order: an order letting US Customs hold shipments suspected of being made with forced labour.
glossary.hs: A customs code that says what a product is. 8541 covers solar cells and panels; 2804.61 is polysilicon.
glossary.sayari: A database of company ownership and shipping records from 250+ countries.
glossary.tradeverifyd: A database of trade relationships between companies, plus risk warnings.
glossary.tavily: A search tool we used to find government notices, research and news.
